harness: existing installed DSH isolated worker, exact worker and launcher hashes bound
prompt: Solve the engineering task specified by spec.md. Return exactly ONE JSON object per turn, no prose or additional actions. Allowed actions: {"tool":"read","file":"spec.md"}, {"tool":"read","file":"accumulator.sv"}, {"tool":"edit","content":"complete file"}, {"tool":"test"}, {"tool":"submit"}. Read both files before edit or submit. Only accumulator.sv can be edited. Test runs the trusted public checker against the current file. You have at most 20 total actions and 4 public tests. Rejected actions also consume an action. Submission is allowed without passing tests and ends solving. Independent terminal and held-out results are not returned. No shell, other files, reference, checker or private inputs are available. Do not combine actions.
stopping_rules: Stop affected cohort on source drift, isolation failure or indeterminate trusted verification; preserve attempt, no replacement.
Each trial ends on submit, 20 actions, worker failure or 1200 seconds.
primary_questions: Does explicit whole-reply rejection permit effective tool interaction?
Were edits actually accepted, and did submitted RTL satisfy the independent reference?

offline_analysis.final_reserved_evaluation: independent finite integer transition oracle after solver stops; separate from formal terminal reward
offline_analysis.training_selection: Do not select trajectories by reserved evaluation

estimated_resources.basis: real formal controls about 3 seconds each; integer anchor about 5 seconds; historical 001 budget study about119k tokens/trial (different task)

interpretation: One new trial per contract, matched task/model/budgets but unpaired provider sampling. Original v1 outcomes remain separate; no stable causal-effect estimate.
reason_for_change: Both first replies combined actions; saturation then had zero accepted edits and repeatedly interpreted generic rejection as broken edit tooling. V2 only explains whole-reply rejection and the next single-action shape; no parsing repair, no execution of bundled actions.
